function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: The unit of measurement for the command execution time, such as 'seconds' or 'milliseconds'

On Windows, the timeout command waits for a specified number of seconds and then exits. We can call it via the function. The function expects a command string. We'll pass "timeout /t 10". But they said "timeout 10". In Windows, you can do "timeout /t 10" or "timeout 10"? Actually, the syntax is "timeout /t <seconds>" but maybe "timeout 10" works? Let's just use "timeout /t 10". The function signature: cmd_controller_execute takes an object with command string and optional unit. We'll provide command: "timeout /t 10". That will wait 10 seconds. Then we return the result.
